clue.text: Return when not in place

parts.note: someone not in is out
to place something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A rule about sending something back whenever it is not where it should be.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory's return is its yield, the amount it produces, so the noun means the same as production.

clue.text: They attract work, models possessing je ne sais quoi

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the models' word contains the other

parts.note: models poses, so poses is the noun here for what models strike
it means that indefinable appeal or charm

explanation.surface: Fashion models with that certain something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'je ne sais quoi' is that indefinable appeal, often called 'it'. The definition plays on the saying that opposites attract.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says opposites attract, so contrary things are the ones that pull towards each other.

clue.text: Like fine lines of article almost prepared

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short by its last letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
ready means prepared

explanation.surface: A newspaper article nearly finished, its text in fine print.
explanation.definitionFit: Thready means thin and thread-like, describing something fine and string-like, such as a weak pulse.

clue.text: Nil desperandum in conflict releasing terrible snarl without restraint

indicators.note: in conflict means the Latin phrase is thrown into disorder
releasing lets the scrambled snarl letters out, terrible marking them as jumbled too

explanation.surface: A motto of never despairing, tested by a terrible tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange NILDESPERANDUM, then remove S, N, A, R, L (the letters of 'snarl'); what is left rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unimpeded means free from hindrance or obstruction, moving with no restraint.

clue.text: Sea creatures get around everything aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the contents on the steamship's letters, so they sit inside them

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: the verb for get goes round the word for everything, enclosing it

parts.note: to cop is to catch or get, informally
all means everything

explanation.surface: Somebody on a boat is told to go round collecting every last item on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get' is the slang verb meaning catch, as a police officer does.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are bivalve shellfish found in the sea, so they are an example of marine creatures.

clue.text: Don't let gems go — they are of great importance

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as an instruction: to corner is to trap and hold, so cornering stones keeps hold of the gems
second meaning: foundations or key elements

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as advice to a jewel owner; split the answer into two words and it is a command to trap the stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornerstone is the essential basis on which something is built, so these are things of fundamental importance.

clue.text: Here it is, exit sign

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look, here it is
to exit is to go

explanation.surface: Someone pointing out the emergency exit sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or symbol representing a company, a kind of sign.

clue.text: Novelty bar in north gets show of approval

indicators.note: bar means except, so these letters are left out

parts.note: an innovation is a novelty
taken as written

explanation.surface: A new bar opening up north wins applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but means 'except', taking IN and N out of INNOVATION.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is a burst of applause, a public demonstration of approval.

clue.text: Fare from Asia heading for touristy area in express

indicators.note: the letters go inside the word for express

parts.note: to express is to say

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of touristy

explanation.surface: Asian food on sale at a tourist spot, served quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'express' looks like 'fast' but is the verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: Satay is a Southeast Asian dish of skewered grilled meat with peanut sauce, so it is Asian food.

clue.text: Biscuit container sealed with clip

indicators.note: the container is closed up inside the clip, which wraps around it

parts.note: a pin clips things together
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: A tin of biscuits kept shut with a clip.
explanation.walkthrough: Parkin is a Northern English gingerbread made with oatmeal and treacle, sometimes baked as biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Parkin is a Yorkshire oatmeal-and-treacle bake, made as a cake or as flat biscuits.

clue.text: One boasts retro attire with good design

indicators.note: retro means backward-looking, so the word for attire is read backwards

parts.note: garb is clothing or attire
art covers design and artistry

explanation.surface: A fashion description: vintage clothing with a nice pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: A braggart is a person who brags, constantly boasting about their own achievements.

clue.text: Nutrient from tea tree hybridised with bacon

indicators.note: hybridised means crossed together, so the letters are combined and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A health product from crossing a tea tree with bacon, absurdly.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta-carotene is a pigment in carrots which the body converts to vitamin A, a nutrient.

clue.text: Disease travelled by water quietly, always retaining force

parts.note: to swim is to travel through water; swam is its past tense

indicators.note: the letters for quietly and always hold the force symbol between them

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
ever means always
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: An illness picked up by someone who swam silently, never letting up their strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Swamp fever is equine infectious anaemia, also a name for malaria or leptospirosis.
explanation.definitionFit: Swamp fever is an illness, a name for equine infectious anaemia and also for malaria caught near marshes.

clue.text: Small split in your trousers

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the phrase holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A little tear in someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun but is a verb, pocketing the letters across 'split in your'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny means very little, so it is a straightforward synonym for small.

clue.text: Win with this shot would make cheerless result

indicators.note: the clue says win joined to this word would make the cheerless word, so the answer is that word with win removed

parts.note: wintry can mean bleak or cheerless, as in a wintry smile
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sports commentator notes that this attempt, had it won, would have changed a gloomy scoreline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win' followed by the answer would make a word meaning cheerless, so the answer is that word minus 'win'. 'result' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a shot at something is to have an attempt, which is what a try is.

clue.text: They provide closure from ties involving street gang

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the word for ties encloses the others

parts.note: a draw is a tied game, so draws are ties
a ring is a criminal gang

explanation.surface: Something about a street gang that drew games against rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawstrings are cords pulled to close a bag or waistband, so they literally provide closure.

clue.text: Got up to pass quickly over rock

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: to zap is to move or go quickly

explanation.surface: Someone stood up to pass a rock at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose topaz is a pink variety of the gemstone topaz, a mineral, so it is a kind of rock.

clue.text: Function with awards entertaining small social gatherings

parts.note: sin is short for sine, a trigonometric function

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so the awards word holds the small letter

parts.note: gongs are medals or awards, informally

explanation.surface: An awards function with small social events laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Function' looks like a party but is the maths sine; gongs is British slang for medals or honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Singsongs are informal gatherings where people sing together.

clue.text: Plants move slowly in pictures from camera

indicators.note: the phrase for moving slowly goes in the word for photographs

parts.note: snaps are photographs
to drag on is to proceed slowly and tediously

explanation.surface: Plants that creep along in time-lapse photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Snapdragons are garden flowers, antirrhinums, so they are an example of plants.

clue.text: First person among fliers dropped over a country

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next letter
dropped means the first-person letter falls further down within the fliers' word

parts.note: airmen are fliers
I is the first person pronoun

explanation.surface: A pilot is dropped over a country from among the airmen.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first-person letter drops lower within the fliers' word, and the result sits over A.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the South Caucasus.

clue.text: Rabbit that may be sweet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pet name for a rabbit, as in bunny
second meaning: often a sweet bread roll

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a cute bunny; the second half is a separate meaning, a small cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bun is a familiar term for a rabbit, and also a small round bread roll, often sweetened, like a currant bun.

clue.text: Cut section of wedding cake and more disconnected

parts.note: a bit is a piece cut off
a tier is one layer of a wedding cake

explanation.surface: Cutting a slice from a wedding cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitty means scrappy and fragmented, so the comparative describes something more fragmented.

clue.text: Hard to escape, bad luck is unchanged

indicators.note: the hard letter escapes, leaving the word for bad luck without it

parts.note: a shame is a pity or bad luck, as in what a shame
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a rut: escaping is hard, and their bad luck persists.
explanation.definitionFit: Same means identical or not altered, so it is a synonym for unchanged.

clue.text: Cancel boat to collect the King

indicators.note: the boat takes the king's letters in, collecting them aboard

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a boat
CR is Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles

explanation.surface: A royal boat trip called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to call it off, an informal synonym for cancel.

clue.text: Pocket set ordered with neat rulers

parts.note: to pot a ball in snooker is to pocket it

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for snooker: pocket a set of balls, arranged neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pocket' is the snooker verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Potentates are monarchs or rulers with great power.

clue.text: Arch nemesis' leader engaged in plot

indicators.note: engaged in means put inside, so it goes into the plot

parts.note: a bed is a garden plot

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of nemesis

explanation.surface: An arch-enemy's chief has a hand in a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch nemesis' reads as a villain, but 'Arch' stands alone as the definition and 'plot' is a garden bed, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curve, and a bend is a curve, so a curved shape fits both.

clue.text: Performed stop before entering road

indicators.note: the words for stop and before go into the road's abbreviation

parts.note: an end is a stop or finish
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A driver halting before pulling onto a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A song or piece of music that is rendered has been performed or interpreted by a musician.

clue.text: Alternative view after exchanging home for short time

indicators.note: exchanging means the word for home is swapped out of the word for view
for names what comes in its place, the brief time abbreviation

parts.note: an opinion is a view
in means at home
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Another point of view, reached after a quick home swap.
explanation.walkthrough: OPINION swaps its IN for T.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is one of several choices available, an alternative.

clue.text: Tea bags with name never used before

indicators.note: bags is a verb, taking hold of the following letters so they sit inside

parts.note: a brew is a cup of tea, informally
and means together with

explanation.surface: Tea bags printed with a brand's name, as yet unused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bags' looks like part of 'tea bags' but is the containing verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand-new means completely fresh and not yet used.

clue.text: Totally unprotected hazy forest region of Portugal

indicators.note: both words lose their outer letters, stripped of their protective covering

explanation.surface: A misty woodland left wholly exposed somewhere in Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are an Atlantic archipelago forming an autonomous region of Portugal.
